name: transactions-bronze-to-gold
description: API to bronze (notebook), then silver and gold (dbt). Decomposed into independently retryable tasks so a failure localises rather than requiring a full re-run.

tasks.description: Fetch from the REST API, validate, quarantine, deduplicate, write Delta bronze, advance the watermark. Imports the repository's validation modules rather than reimplementing them.
Build stg_transactions (silver) and daily_account_summary (gold), then run 32 data tests and the enforced model contract.

_notes.why_two_tasks: Ingestion and transformation fail for different reasons and are owned differently. Splitting them means a transient API failure retries the fetch without rebuilding the mart, and a failing dbt test does not re-hit the API. One long script cannot do either.
_notes.why_retries_differ: Ingestion retries three times because API failures are usually transient. dbt retries once because a failing data quality test is not transient - it means the data is wrong and a human should look.
_notes.why_max_concurrent_runs_1: The watermark is shared mutable state. Two concurrent runs could both read the same value and one would overwrite the other's advance.
_notes.why_health_rule: A run taking far longer than usual is a leading indicator of source degradation, visible before an outright failure.
_notes.not_deployed: This definition is committed as documentation of the intended orchestration. The notebook and the dbt project were both executed manually against a live workspace; the Job wrapper itself was not deployed.
